text: dsh-attachment-s3 是面向 DSH 的 S3 兼容图片附件存储后端，通过 Cordis 的附件存储接口接管会话图片，并在 bundle patch 中停用本地附件后端。它将规范化后的图片写入单一 bucket，以 SHA-256 内容地址组织对象，重复内容可汇聚到同一对象；读取时重新核对摘要和图像元数据。插件也支持按请求策略生成图片版本并缓存在本机。适合希望把 DSH 图片附件放到对象存储、供部署集中管理的场景；需要配置 bucket，并可使用 AWS 凭据链或凭据引用。

dsh-attachment-s3 stores DSH image attachments in an S3-compatible bucket, replacing the local backend. Images use SHA-256 content addresses; reads verify bytes and metadata. It derives request-sized variants and caches them locally. Configure a bucket and AWS credentials or credential references.

How can I store DSH image attachments in an S3 bucket?
I want content-addressed storage with verified reads for session images.
图片附件以规范化后的字节计算 SHA-256，并按摘要写入 bucket；相同内容使用相同对象地址，引用保存摘要标识。
读取时按引用限定字节范围，重新计算 SHA-256 并检查图像格式和尺寸；数据与引用不符时返回损坏附件错误。
模型请求可按请求策略从存储图像派生尺寸与编码版本，并将可复现的派生图像缓存到本机目录。
S3 客户端可从凭据服务或环境变量按引用解析访问凭据；也可省略引用，使用 AWS SDK 自带的凭据链。
运行时必须配置 bucket；bundle 会停用本地附件后端并替换为该 S3 后端。
对象写入后插件没有保留期或删除流程；生命周期规则若提前清理仍被会话引用的对象，读取会得到未找到结果。

dsh-attachment-s3 README · dsh-attachment-s3：S3 storage for the DeepSeek Harness attachment seam. It implements [`AttachmentStore`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/master/packages/attachment/attachment) — the same abstract service the in-box `@deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment-local` backend implements over `DSH_HOME` — so a deployment's session images live in a bucket instead of on the machine that admitted them. The seam takes exactly one provider, so this plugin replaces the local backend rather than joining it.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · dsh-attachment-s3：Nothing about the bucket is model-visible: the durable reference stays the opaque `sha256:` id already recorded in the session log, so moving between backends does not change what a transcript means.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-attachment-s3
export DSH_ATTACHMENT_S3_BUCKET=my-attachments
export DSH_ATTACHMENT_S3_REGION=us-east-1
dsh --profile <name>

The package declares `"dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" } }`, so `dsh plugin` appends it to the profile's bundle layer stack. Its patch disables the `attachment-local` row `dsh-base` inserts and adds the `attachment-s3` row. Check both before booting:

dsh-attachment-s3 README · Install：```sh
dsh --profile <name> --dump-config | grep -A2 'id: attachment'
```

`dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-attachment-s3` reverses the install and restores the local backend.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · Environment：The bundle patch reads its values from the environment at mount. `DSH_`-prefixed names must come from the launching environment — `export` them or set them in the unit that starts dsh; the launcher refuses that prefix inside a `.env` file. Credential *values* are yours to name, so they can live in `$DSH_HOME/.env`.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · Environment：To pin configuration instead of reading the environment, restate the row in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml`, which is applied after every bundle layer. An id-targeted patch replaces the row's whole `config`, so restate the fields you keep:

```yaml
- id: attachment-s3
  name: 'dsh-attachment-s3'
  config:
    bucket: my-attachments

dsh-attachment-s3 README · Configuration：Admission, normalization, and request-image derivation are delegated to the in-box `@deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment-local` package, which exports them as plain functions; the defaults above are re-exported from it rather than restated. That keeps one encoder policy across both backends — the same image is accepted, stored, and put in front of a model either way — and leaves this package owning only the bucket. Object policy a bucket already owns — default encryption, storage class, lifecycle — is left to the bucket.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · Configuration：Configuration carries credential **references**, never values, matching the harness [credential seam](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/master/packages/credentials/credentials). Each is resolved per request, through `ctx.credentials` when a credential provider is loaded and through the process environment otherwise, so a rotated secret reaches the next request without a restart. Declare both key references or neither: a half-declared pair fails at load instead of silently signing as the SDK's ambient identity. Declaring neither is the normal deployment on an instance role.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · How it stores：```
<prefix>/objects/<first two hex digits>/<sha256 hex>
```

One immutable object per distinct image, `Content-Type` set to the verified media type, the SHA-256 sent as the object checksum, and the intrinsic `width`/`height` recorded as object metadata. The session log records `sha256:<hex>` — an opaque id, never a key or a URL. The `v1` segment fences a future incompatible layout off from stored objects.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · How it stores：What lands in the bucket is the **normalized** image, not the submitted bytes: admission downscales a large source to the stored long edge and re-encodes it under a byte budget, and the reference records the original dimensions. The version a model request carries is derived from the stored object on demand and cached locally, since it is reproducible and does not belong in the bucket.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · How it stores：- **Content addressing does the deduplicating.** The key is the SHA-256 of the bytes being written, so a save that finds the key taken rewrites exactly what is already there, and the reference it publishes describes bytes that same call wrote. Two writers of one image converge on one object; only the upload repeats. Every upload also sends `x-amz-checksum-sha256`, so a service that verifies it rejects bytes that arrived damaged.
- **Verified reads.** A read requests exactly the byte range the reference claims, re-hashes the bytes, and re-derives the image header before returning, so a bucket-side substitution surfaces as `ATTACHMENT_CORRUPT` instead of reaching a model request.
- **Failure codes.** Admission keeps the seam's caller-correctable codes (`IMAGE_TOO_LARGE`, `IMAGE_TYPE_MISMATCH`, `IMAGE_TOO_MANY_PIXELS`, `IMAGE_DIMENSION_TOO_LARGE`, `INVALID_IMAGE`); storage failures surface as `ATTACHMENT_WRITE_FAILED`, `ATTACHMENT_READ_FAILED`, `ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND`, or `ATTACHMENT_CORRUPT`, each carrying its cause.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · S3-compatible services：The backend needs three things from a bucket: an upload that accepts a SHA-256 checksum header, ranged reads, and a distinguishable "no such key". Probe a service before pointing a deployment at it:

```sh
PROBE_ENDPOINT=https://s3.example.com PROBE_REGION=us-east-1 PROBE_BUCKET=<bucket> \
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=... AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... pnpm run probe
```

dsh-attachment-s3 README · S3-compatible services：It writes and deletes two small objects and reports what the service does with each behavior, including whether a wrong checksum is actually rejected or merely accepted. A service that rejects the checksum header cannot run this backend as it stands.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · Development：```sh
pnpm install       # runs `prepare`, which builds lib/
pnpm run test      # unit tests, including the real AWS SDK against a loopback S3-compatible service
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run build

dsh-attachment-s3 README · Development：`pnpm run test` needs no bucket and no network: `tests/support/fake-s3.ts` serves the S3 requests the SDK actually sends, so signing, checksum headers, range reads, and status classification are exercised for real. The e2e suite reads `DSH_S3_E2E_BUCKET` and optionally `DSH_S3_E2E_REGION`, `DSH_S3_E2E_ENDPOINT`, `DSH_S3_E2E_FORCE_PATH_STYLE`, and `DSH_S3_E2E_PREFIX`; it writes under a random per-run prefix and deletes what it wrote.
dsh-attachment-s3 README · Development：Publishing runs `prepublishOnly` first: clean, typecheck, the full suite, then build.

dsh-attachment-s3 README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **No retention or deletion.** Objects are written and never removed; the seam has no retention policy on either backend. Bucket lifecycle rules are the only collector, and expiring an object a session still references turns that attachment into `ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND`.
- **Images only.** The seam's version-one surface carries PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF.
- **One bucket per deployment.** Routing sessions or workspaces to different buckets would need a routing layer this package does not have.
- **Full-object transfers.** Reads buffer the whole image in memory, bounded by `maxImageBytes`.
- **Sharing needs more than attachments.** Session logs stay wherever the profile's persistence backend puts them — by default `$DSH_HOME/sessions`, which is machine-local. A bucket makes attachments durable and centrally managed; it does not by itself make a session readable from another machine.
